page.layout: One column of running text, with the page number and running head at the top right and left. No margin notes, no footnotes. The catchword stands alone at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: contrariam doctrinam discordiae matricem inter Magistratum & ministerium esse; & causam justissimae indignationis Magistratus contra pastores, quae suo tempore in iram & & vindictam ipsi à Deo imperatam erumpit. Atque hinc perpetuo illa doctrina à nostris Theologis pro seditiosâ & contumeliosâ in Magistratus habita fuit, prout facile ostendere possem. Quod autem dicunt Pontificii, eos qui nostram hanc doctrinam profitentur Schisma moliri in Ecclesiâ, icipsum falsissimum est.

E contrario doctrina adversariorum verè schismatica est, utpote quam Donatus, schismatis perniciosissimi in Ecclesiâ vetere autor, primus professus est. Quemadmodum etiam dubium non est, quin si aliquis nostris Ecclesiis contrariam doctrinam proponeret, Schisma quantum in se est efficeret, dum opiniones verbo Dei contrarias, & in Ecclesiis nostris non receptas invehere conaretur: cui machi-[?]

page.notes: The section marker beside the running head reads "§. XIV." (the sign is set in an unusual form; the "§" reading is uncertain). "icipsum" is printed as shown and is probably a printing error for "ipsum". "machi-" at the foot is the catchword and its ending is uncertain. The word "in iram &" is followed by a repeated "&" as printed. The scan is faint in places, but no words are illegible.
